Collector's notes
Appraising waifu figures
Put the figure in the tray and look at it through the magnifier. Its value depends on its rarity (on the label) and on the marks on the next pages.
Base value by rarity
Common: 60₵
Rare: 180₵
Epic: 450₵
Legendary: 1200₵
Order: 1. check the seal (fake or gold star?). 2. condition and paint. 3. gloss edition. All deductions and bonuses are fixed amounts you add to the base value.
1. Seal of authenticity
Every genuine figure has a star on the front of its base, right of centre, with a white or a golden rim. Take a close look with the magnifier.
Genuine: holo star
Fake: dull and grey
Fake: round, not a star
Fake: no seal
The gold star is the collector's seal of a limited edition: +100₵ on the base value. A fake, on the other hand, is only ever worth 20₵, however rare or pretty it looks otherwise.
2. Condition and paint
Genuine figures only. Look over the whole body: damage is small and easy to miss.
Scratches in the paint: −20₵
Crack in the material: −80₵
Smeared paint (factory error): −40₵
A figure has either scratches or a crack. A paint error can come on top.
3. Gloss edition
Golden sparkles on the figure: limited gloss edition. +150₵ (genuine figures only).
Example
Epic figure with a gold star, scratches in the paint, golden sparkles.
At least 10₵. Within 5 % is a perfect appraisal. Too far off and the Geek turns it down.
